coreStatement.content: A recursive algorithm solves a problem by reducing it to smaller instances of the same problem.

eqLabel.content: The Recurrence Model — hover each term

whyRecurrence.content: A recurrence translates the recursive structure of an algorithm into a mathematical equation, so its asymptotic behaviour can be derived rather than guessed.

rows.question: What is a recurrence relation?
rows.answer: An equation that defines the cost of a recursive algorithm in terms of the cost of its own smaller subproblems, together with the work done outside the recursive calls.

rows.question: Why is a base case necessary?
rows.answer: It is the condition at which reduction stops. Without it the recursion never terminates and the call stack grows without bound.

rows.name: Recursive Case
rows.detail: Defines how the current problem is reduced into smaller subproblems of the same form.

rows.name: Base Case
rows.detail: Defines the condition at which the reduction stops and recursion terminates.

rows.name: Reduction Factor
rows.detail: Describes how quickly the problem size decreases at each recursive step.

rows.label: T(n) — Total Cost
rows.meaning: The running time required by the algorithm on an input of size n. This is the quantity the recurrence defines.

rows.label: The Recurrence
rows.meaning: T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n) expresses the cost of a recursive computation in terms of the cost of its own smaller subproblems.

rows.label: a — Number of Subproblems
rows.meaning: How many recursive calls the algorithm makes at each level of the recursion.

rows.label: n/b — Reduced Input
rows.meaning: The size of each subproblem: b is the factor by which the input is divided at every recursive step.

rows.label: Composition of Cost
rows.meaning: Total cost is the recursive work plus the work done outside the recursive calls at that level.

rows.label: f(n) — Non-Recursive Work
rows.meaning: Work performed outside the recursive calls: setup, comparisons, partitioning, scanning, and combining results.

rows.name: Recursion Tree
rows.detail: Expands the recursive calls level by level and sums the work performed at each level.

rows.name: Substitution
rows.detail: Proposes a solution form for T(n) and verifies the bound mathematically.

rows.name: Standard Results
rows.detail: Recognises established recurrence patterns and applies their known asymptotic bounds.
